# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The manual maps each light color to a wire of the identical color. I need convey the equality pattern to Deaf through gestures; repeated paired symbols can represent “first matches first, second matches second, third matches third.” Deaf can then describe the matching-color rule aloud to Blind, who can identify the light and wires by touch only if the bomb provides distinguishable features or Deaf supplies the visible color.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👍", "👎", "👎", "👌", "👌"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I can cut wire positions 1, 2, or 3. Please read the manual and tell me what tactile information you need from me and the exact cutting rule.
Deaf says to Mute: Bomb view: display 0; light yellow; wires in order 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. I received your gestures: thumbs-up thumbs-up, thumbs-down thumbs-down, OK OK. Please provide the manual rule or a code meaning.

The visible bomb has a yellow light, and the manual says to cut the same color: yellow. Deaf reports that yellow is wire position 2. Blind can act only on a spoken instruction from Deaf, so I will use the conventional two-finger gesture to mean “cut wire 2”; Deaf should relay that instruction aloud to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports: display 0; light yellow; wires: position 1 red, position 2 yellow, position 3 blue. Please give the exact safe cut position or any further required rule.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✌ 👉 👍 👎]
Deaf says to Mute: I see your two-finger gesture. Does it mean Blind should act on wire 2? Reply thumbs-up for yes, thumbs-down for no.

The manual rule confirms that a yellow light requires cutting the yellow wire. Deaf’s visual report places the yellow wire at position 2, so Deaf’s interpretation is correct. I will confirm it.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf says you gestured two fingers, possibly meaning wire 2, but it is unconfirmed. Please say aloud: 'cut wire 1', 'cut wire 2', or 'cut wire 3' if that is your manual instruction. I will not act on an ambiguous gesture.
Deaf says to Mute: I have told Blind to cut wire 2, the yellow wire.

Blind cannot receive my gestures directly, and I cannot speak. Deaf has already relayed the correct instruction. The yellow light maps to the yellow wire, which is wire 2; I will again confirm Deaf’s instruction so Deaf can state it plainly to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✌"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Deaf says to Mute: Update: wire 2 was cut correctly. New state: blue light; wire 1 red intact, wire 2 cut, wire 3 blue intact. I received thumbs-up then two-finger gesture. Please clarify the required next action.

The bomb now has a blue light. The manual requires cutting the blue wire, and Deaf identifies that as intact wire position 3. I will use the three-extended-fingers gesture as the next-position instruction, consistent with the earlier two-finger gesture for wire 2.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Current state remains: blue light; wire 1 red intact, wire 2 cut, wire 3 blue intact. I received the horn-hand gesture. What action does it specify? If it means a wire, please signal its number unambiguously and confirm yes with thumbs-up.

The horn gesture was not an established numeral, so it was ambiguous. The required action is wire 3: blue light maps to blue wire, and Deaf identifies the intact blue wire as position 3. I will make the number explicit by repeating the same gesture exactly three times, followed by thumbs-up as confirmation.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆", "👆", "👆", "👍"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: I interpret your three upward-pointing gestures plus thumbs-up as confirmed wire 3 and have told Blind to cut it.

Deaf’s interpretation is correct: blue light requires cutting the blue wire, which is position 3. I confirm that instruction.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Deaf says to Mute: Update: wire 3 was cut correctly. New state: red light; wire 1 red remains intact, wires 2 and 3 are cut. Please send the next required action.

The red light requires cutting the red wire. The only intact red wire is position 1. Using the established repeated upward-pointing count, one upward-pointing gesture means wire 1, followed by confirmation.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆", "👍"])
```

TURN 9
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: I interpret one upward-pointing gesture plus thumbs-up as confirmed wire 1 and have instructed Blind to cut it.

Deaf’s interpretation is correct: the red light maps to the red wire at position 1. I confirm the cut instruction.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```
